```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal is a single paying customer. B's buyer is an individual paying $8–24/mo with a card, with no procurement step. A's own brief says buyers expect SOC 2, DPA, or EU AI Act evidence and see trusting an unproven one-person vendor with destructive-action gating as a high bar. That directly obstructs a first sale.",
    "B names a quantified, low-cost channel for reaching a first buyer: Meta lead ads at about $12.30 per lead, with Google Career & Employment cost per lead down roughly 46.7% year over year from $117.92. These numbers are too costly to sustain at scale given the low lifetime value, but they are affordable for landing one customer. A's channels are a free Show HN launch with no sourced outcome data, or a TLDR sponsorship needing a $9,000 minimum (3 issues at $3,000).",
    "B's build is a bounded text pipeline (parse resume, find gaps, generate a roadmap) with low trust stakes per user. A's product sits inside production execution paths, where one bug causes the very harm it is meant to prevent. That raises both build risk and reputational risk for a solo operator running AI agents.",
    "B is less crowded on the evidence given: five named competitors, of which one (WeGoUp) is pre-alpha and one (CoachGPT) has pricing NOT FOUND. A has nine or more live competitors, several with free tiers and a fully free open-source package.",
    "B's regulatory setup is a one-time 2–4 hour privacy consult plus implementing deletion. A's brief calls SOC 2 Type II a de facto requirement costing multiple months and thousands of dollars, which no solo founder can meet within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A says self-serve pricing of $19–199/mo is 'already proven viable by multiple live competitors.' That claim rests only on published pricing pages. Nothing in the brief shows any competitor has paying customers at those tiers, and JamJet has no public price at all. A's SOC 2 buyer-expectation claim and its AgentBoundary spec reference are also given without any citation.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low. Neither brief shows evidence of actual conversion or willingness to pay. Both rely on price pages and anecdotal forum quotes. A has stronger evidence of acute pain (a documented production incident plus developer quotes), and a high-value B2B buyer could make it the better long-term business. B's weaknesses are real but bear more on long-term economics than on the 90-day first-customer goal: one-time need, low lifetime value, a price-sensitive segment, and harm risk around sensitive health and caregiving gaps. B wins mainly because its path to a first payment faces fewer trust and compliance barriers."
}
```
